points: The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah and dwell among the people in the wilderness of Judah.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and goes up with ten thousand men at his feet, and Deborah goes up with him. Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites and pitched his tent by Kedesh.

Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water.

Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People
